title: Best Running Shoes for Wide Feet
excerpt: Running shoes made in wide and extra-wide widths: Brooks Ghost 18 and Adrenaline GTS 25, New Balance 880v15, Hoka Bondi 9 and Brooks Cascadia 19.
body:
Best Running Shoes for Wide Feet

Updated November 2026. Prices are US list prices (MSRP) at the time of this update; retailers often sell for less.

If standard running shoes squeeze your forefoot, choose a model made in wide widths rather than going up a size. Sizing up adds length, which moves the shoe's flex point and widest part away from where your foot needs them. Every shoe below is available in wide widths, as confirmed by the brand or a major retailer. Prices are US list prices (MSRP) at the time of this update.

Width sizing, briefly

Brooks labels men's wide as 2E and men's extra wide as 4E. Women's width letters differ from men's, so check the brand's size chart. Widths also vary between brands, so a "wide" in one brand may fit differently in another.

The picks

Brooks Ghost 18: best overall

The Brooks Ghost 18 lists at $150. It comes in narrow, medium, wide and extra wide for men and women. It's a cushioned, neutral daily trainer that launched in June 2026, replacing the Ghost 17.

Brooks Adrenaline GTS 25: wide with stability

The Brooks Adrenaline GTS 25 is Brooks's stability trainer and comes in wide and extra-wide widths. Its successor, the Adrenaline GTS 26 ($155), is on preorder at Brooks, so check which version is available when you buy.

New Balance Fresh Foam X 880v15: wide and extra wide, lower drop

The New Balance 880v15 lists at $140 and is made in wide and extra-wide sizes. It has a 6 mm drop, lower than many traditional trainers.

Hoka Bondi 9: maximum cushion

The Hoka Bondi 9 lists at $175 and comes in wide and extra-wide sizes. It has a heel stack of about 43 mm and a 5 mm drop.

Brooks Cascadia 19: trail option

The Brooks Cascadia 19 lists at $170. It's offered in a wide width for men. Women's wide availability varies by retailer, so check before you buy.

Fit tips for wide feet

  • Measure both feet standing up, late in the day, and fit the larger foot.
  • Check the toe box shape as well as the width label. A tapered toe box can pinch even in a wide.
  • Loosen or skip lace eyelets over any pressure point.
  • Leave about a thumb's width in front of your longest toe.
